applicable_when: The kernel is a strided scatter: reads contiguous floats from in_ptr0 and writes to out_ptr0 with stride-256 store pattern (index: x0 + 256*x1). This non-contiguous write causes severe L1TEX stalls — 21.7 cycles average, 52.4% of all stall cycles. The scheduler has no eligible warp 75.92% of cycles. With only 1960 CTAs across 132 SMs (0.93 waves) and XBLOCK=128 (4 warps per block), there are too few in-flight warps to hide L1TEX latency. Increasing num_warps from 4 to 8 doubles the warps per CTA, giving the scheduler more warps to switch to while others wait on L1TEX. This is a pure launch-parameter change — no kernel body modification — so it cannot cause the correctness failures seen in prior XBLOCK-autotune attempts. Registers per thread is only 16, so doubling warps (128→256 threads/block) still fits within the 2048 threads/SM limit.
